day-1.t: Day 1 — Write for one person with one problem

b.v: Today's goal

v: Describe your one ideal buyer in plain words
Find the problem they feel at the moment they read
Stop writing to 'everyone'

b.v: About 20 minutes. You need one page and a pen. Write by hand first; it is slower and better.

Copywriting means writing words that cause an action: click, message, order. It is not clever writing. Clever writing makes people admire the writer. Good copy makes people recognise themselves and take the next step.
1) One person, not a crowd
Writing for everyone produces sentences nobody feels. Writing for one person produces sentences that thousands recognise.

Write this in your notebook:|Their age range and city area|Their job and roughly their monthly income|What they were doing five minutes before they saw your ad|The exact words they use for the problem, in Urdu or English|What they are afraid of losing if they choose badly

Example for a Karachi sewing machine shop: 'Sana, 31, lives in North Nazimabad, stitches clothes at home for neighbours, earns about Rs 25,000 a month, and is afraid of buying a machine that jams after two months.' Now every sentence has a job.
2) Sell the change, not the object
Nobody wants a machine. They want finished orders before Friday and no repair bill. Nobody wants a three-piece suit; they want to walk into the wedding looking like they made an effort.

v: Feature = what it is: a 1.5 ton inverter AC
Benefit = what it does for them: a bedroom cool enough to sleep in, with a bill you can predict
Proof = why they should believe you: three years of the same model in your own shop
Offer = what they get if they act now: free installation this week

b.v: 3) The four questions every buyer has
In their head, quietly, every buyer asks the same four things. Your copy answers them in order.
Answer these on the page:|What exactly is this?|Why should I care today?|Why you and not the shop down the road?|What happens if I order and it is wrong?

Do not open with your company history, your founder's dream or 'Welcome to our website'. Nobody is looking for you. They are looking for a solution, and you have about two seconds before they scroll on.
Practice

Do this now:|Write the six line buyer profile from step 1|Write one sentence: 'My buyer is afraid that ___'|Rewrite that sentence as the first line of your product page|Read it aloud. If it sounds like a brochure, write it again like a message to a friend.

day-2.t: Day 2 — Product descriptions that answer the buyer

b.v: Today's goal

v: Write a description with the six parts buyers need
Use exact sizes, materials and delivery facts
Write a second version for a phone screen

b.v: About 20 minutes. Pick one real product you sell and finish its description today.

A product description is a salesperson that works all night. It must answer questions before they become doubts, because a doubt is a closed tab. Vague words like 'premium quality' answer nothing and cost you sales.
1) The six parts
Use the same six parts for every product. It becomes fast, and customers always find what they need.

v: One line saying what it is and who it is for
Three to five facts: size, material, weight, colour options
What it solves, in the buyer's words
What is included and what is not
Delivery time, charges and return rule
One clear next step with a phone or button

b.v: 2) Show the writing, not just the advice
Here is a weak description and a working one for the same item. This is the difference the whole lesson is about.

@Text
WEAK:
Premium quality unstitched lawn suit. Best fabric. Beautiful design. Order now!

WORKING:
Unstitched 3-piece lawn suit, summer weight, for daily wear.
- Shirt: 2.5 metres printed lawn
- Dupatta: 2.5 metres chiffon
- Trouser: 2.5 metres cambric
- Colours: navy, maroon, off-white
Washes well by hand, colour holds after repeated wash.
Rs 3,850. Delivery in Lahore Rs 200, 2 to 3 days. Other cities 3 to 5 days.
Not stitched. Stitching is Rs 1,200 extra if you send measurements on WhatsApp.
Message us the colour and your city to confirm stock.
Every line removes a question. Metres, colours, wash care, price, delivery, stitching, next step. Nothing is invented and nothing is padded.
3) Write for a thumb
Most buyers read on a phone, standing, in a hurry. Short paragraphs, one idea per line, and the price visible without hunting.

Mobile edit:|Cut every sentence over 15 words|Put the price in the first three lines|Turn specs into a short list, not a paragraph|Replace 'contact us for details' with the actual detail|Check that the first screen alone makes sense

Do not copy a description from a supplier or another shop. It is usually wrong for your stock, it competes with the original in search, and it can be a copyright problem. Also never write a size or material you have not checked with your own hands.
Practice

Do this now:|Choose your best selling product|Write all six parts, using real measurements|Read it on your phone and cut anything over 15 words|Ask one customer: does anything here leave you with a question?|Fix that gap in the description

day-3.t: Day 3 — Captions for Facebook and Instagram

b.v: Today's goal

v: Write the first line so people stop scrolling
Use a structure that ends in a message, not a like
Write three captions for three different jobs

b.v: About 20 minutes. Keep your phone open; you will post one today.

A caption is not a description of the photo. The photo already shows the thing. The caption's job is to give a reason to act: price, scarcity that is real, a doubt answered, or a story the buyer recognises.
1) The first line does the work
Only the first line or two shows before 'more'. If the first line is 'Alhamdulillah new stock available', nobody taps more. Start with the buyer's thought.

v: Start with the problem: 'School shoes that survive a full term are rare.'
Start with the price: 'Rs 2,450, stitched, delivered.'
Start with the objection: 'Yes, this lawn does not shrink. We washed one.'
Avoid starting with 'We are pleased to announce'

b.v: 2) A structure you can reuse

Write in this order:|Hook: one line about their situation|Detail: what it is, with the real price|Proof: a fact, a review line, a number of years|Action: 'Message us the size and city'|Then stop. No 20 hashtags, no five emojis in a row.

Example: 'Eid is in three weeks and the tailor is already saying no. We stitch in 5 days, Rs 1,200, and we send photos before delivery. Message your measurements today.' That is a hook, a detail, proof of speed, and an action.
3) Three captions, three jobs

v: Selling caption = price, stock, action. Use when you want orders today.
Story caption = how a customer used it, or why you started. Builds trust between selling posts.
Answer caption = replies to a common question, such as delivery charges. Saves you repeating yourself.

b.v: Do not write 'limited stock' every day. Fake scarcity works once and destroys trust after that. If you say three pieces left, there should be three pieces left. Also do not use copied captions from other pages: your customers follow them too.
Practice

Do this now:|Write one hook line about a real customer problem|Write the three captions: selling, story, answer|Post the selling one with a real photo and a real price|Note the time. If nobody messages, the first line is the first thing to change.

day-4.t: Day 4 — Landing page structure that carries the reader

b.v: Today's goal

v: Lay out a page in the order a buyer thinks
Write each section in one or two sentences
Remove the things that distract from the next step

b.v: About 25 minutes. You can do this on paper before touching the website.
A landing page is one page with one job. Every extra link, menu item and pop-up is another door out of the shop. Structure is not decoration; it is the order in which doubts are removed.
1) The order

Build the page like this:|Headline: the result, in their words|One line under it: who it is for and the price|Proof strip: years, jobs done, a review line|Three benefits as short blocks, not a wall of text|What is included, in a list|Price and offer, plainly|Objections, answered in three lines|One final action, repeated|Small print: delivery, returns, contact
2) Write like a person explaining, not a company announcing
Short sentences. Active voice. The word 'you' more often than the word 'we'.

Before: 'Our company is committed to providing high quality solutions for all your needs.' After: 'We fit your kitchen in 6 days. You get a fixed price before we start.' The second one is shorter, concrete and about the customer.
3) Remove the exits

v: Remove the top menu on a paid landing page
Remove social icons. They lead away for free.
Remove the side bar and the 'recent posts'
Remove any form field you do not truly need
Keep one primary button colour, used only for the main action

b.v: Do not hide the price to 'get more enquiries'. In most small local markets, hiding the price brings people who cannot afford it and wastes your time on the phone. If the price varies, give the range and say what moves it.
Practice

Do this now:|Sketch your page in nine boxes on paper|Write the headline and the one line under it|List three objections a buyer would have and answer each in a sentence|Open your real page and remove one thing that is not helping|Read the page on your phone from top to bottom once

day-5.t: Day 5 — Headlines: ten words that decide everything

b.v: Today's goal

v: Write 10 headlines for one offer
Use four reliable patterns
Choose one with a test, not a feeling

b.v: About 20 minutes. Write all ten before judging any of them.

Most people read the headline and nothing else. If the headline is vague, the rest of the page is never seen. Ten mediocre headlines are worth less than one clear one, so write many and keep the clearest.
1) Four patterns that keep working

v: Result: 'A cool bedroom in 20 minutes, without changing your wiring'
Problem: 'Tailor saying no before Eid? We stitch in 5 days.'
Number: 'Kitchen fitted in 6 days, fixed price before we start'
Direct: 'Iron gates made to size in Lahore, from Rs 45,000'

b.v: Each pattern is honest and specific. Notice that none of them uses words like 'best', 'quality' or 'solutions'. Those words are invisible because everyone uses them.
2) Make it specific

Specific numbers and places make a claim believable. Compare 'Fast delivery all over Pakistan' with 'Order before 4 pm, delivered in Karachi tomorrow, Rs 250'. The second one is a promise you can keep and a customer can check.

Improve a weak headline:|Write the vague version first, honestly|Underline every vague word, such as quality, best, trusted|Replace each with a fact: a number, a time, a place, a price|Read it to someone and ask what exactly is being sold|If they cannot answer, rewrite
3) Keep the promise you print
A headline is a promise. If it says 5 days, the order must arrive in 5 days. The fastest way to kill a business is a strong headline with a weak delivery.

Do not use a headline you cannot prove, such as 'Number 1 in Pakistan' or 'The cheapest in the city'. Claims like that invite complaints, and in advertising they can be treated as misleading. Say what you can show: '3,000 orders since 2019'.
Practice

Do this now:|Write 10 headlines for one product using the four patterns|Cross out every vague word|Choose your top two|Send both to five customers on WhatsApp and ask which they understand faster|Use the winner, and note the result

day-6.t: Day 6 — Offers: making the price feel fair

b.v: Today's goal

v: Build an offer, not just a discount
Use risk reversal without lying
Present price so the value is obvious

b.v: About 20 minutes. Bring your real costs. An offer built on a guess loses money quietly.

An offer is what the buyer gets, for how much, with what risk, by when. A discount is only one way to make an offer. Often the better move is to remove risk or add something cheap that the buyer values.
1) The four parts of an offer

v: What they get: the product plus anything included
Price and payment: total, and whether JazzCash, Easypaisa or cash on delivery is fine
Risk: what happens if it is wrong, late or damaged
Deadline: a real reason to act now, such as Eid stock arriving

b.v: Example, using made-up but realistic numbers: 'Kitchen fitting, Rs 185,000 including cabinets, hinges and labour. 50 percent on order, rest on completion. If we are late, Rs 2,000 off per day. Book this month and we include the sink.' That is a complete offer with a real guarantee.
2) Risk reversal is usually stronger than a discount

A Rs 2,000 discount saves a little money. 'If the size is wrong, we exchange it free within 7 days' removes a fear. Fear stops more sales than price does, especially for online orders paid by JazzCash.

Add one honest risk reducer:|Exchange within a stated number of days, with conditions you can afford|Free measurement before payment|Cash on delivery where you can manage it|A written delivery date, with what happens if you miss it|A photo of the exact item before dispatch
3) Show the price next to something
A number alone feels expensive. A number next to a comparison feels reasonable. Use true comparisons only.

Honest framing: 'Rs 1,200 to stitch a suit. A ready-made suit of this fabric costs more and will not fit you.' Dishonest framing: 'Worth Rs 10,000, yours for Rs 1,200' when it was never sold at Rs 10,000.

Do not invent a fake original price and cut it. Do not say 'free delivery' and add the charge into the price without telling the customer; that is the same lie with better manners. And do not promise a guarantee you cannot afford to honour when ten customers claim it.
Practice

Do this now:|Write your current offer in the four parts|Add one risk reducer you can genuinely honour|Check the maths on your profit after that promise|Rewrite your price line with a true comparison|Put the offer on your product page and in your WhatsApp quick reply
Today's goal

v: Collect proof you already have
List the five real objections and answer each
Place answers where the doubt appears

b.v: About 20 minutes. Most shops already own more proof than they use.

People believe evidence, not adjectives. 'High quality' is an opinion. 'Same stitching machine used for 6 years, 400 suits, one repair' is evidence. Objections are not insults; they are the last step before buying.
1) Proof you already have

v: Screenshots of real WhatsApp thank-you messages, with names hidden
Photos of finished work, especially messy before and clean after
Numbers: years in business, orders delivered, repeat customers
Names of areas you have delivered to
A short video of the workshop or shop, unstaged
A guarantee in writing

b.v: Ask three past customers for one line you can quote, and ask permission to use their first name and area. 'Ayesha, Gulshan, ordered twice' is enough. Nobody needs a full testimonial with a photo.
2) The five objections
Nearly every objection is one of these five. Write your answer once and reuse it everywhere.

Answer these on your page and in your messages:|Too expensive: explain what is included and what cheap versions lack|Will it fit or suit me: give exact measurements and an exchange rule|Can I trust you: proof, address, a phone number a human answers|What if it is late: a real delivery window and what happens if missed|I will think about it: a small, honest reason to decide now
3) Put the answer where the doubt is
Proof on a separate 'About us' page is nearly useless. Put the delivery promise next to the price, the exchange rule next to the size chart, and the review next to the buy button.

Do not invent testimonials, and do not edit a customer's words into something they did not say. If a customer complains publicly, answer plainly and fix it. A visible, well-handled complaint builds more trust than ten perfect reviews.
Practice

Do this now:|List five objections you hear on the phone|Write a one or two line answer for each|Collect three real proof items today|Place one proof item beside your price|Reply publicly to your oldest unanswered review

day-8.t: Day 8 — WhatsApp sales messages that do not feel like spam

b.v: Today's goal

v: Write a first reply that moves the sale forward
Handle the three messages that kill deals
Use templates without sounding like a robot

b.v: About 20 minutes. In Pakistan, most sales are decided in this chat, not on the website.

A WhatsApp chat is a conversation with a stranger who is interested but not yet convinced. Your job is to answer, reassure and make the next step tiny. Long paragraphs and slow replies lose more sales than price does.
1) The first reply
Answer the question, add the one fact they will ask next, and offer a clear next step. Three lines, not three paragraphs.

@WhatsApp
Customer: Price?

Reply:
Rs 3,850 for the 3-piece, unstitched.
Delivery Rs 200 in Lahore, 2 to 3 days. Stitching Rs 1,200 extra.
Which colour do you want? I will send a photo of the actual piece.
Notice what happened: price given immediately, delivery and stitching answered before being asked, and a small question at the end that keeps the conversation alive.
2) Three difficult messages

v: 'Too expensive' = do not argue. Explain what is included and offer the smaller option if you have one.
'I will let you know' = accept it, then ask one useful question: 'Which part are you unsure about, the size or the price?'
'Is this original?' = answer with evidence, such as a photo of the label, the bill, or your supplier's name if you may share it

b.v: 3) Templates that still sound human
Build five quick replies:|Price and what is included|Delivery time and charges by city|Size or measurement help|Payment methods, including JazzCash and Easypaisa|A polite follow-up after two days

Then edit each one before sending: add the customer's name and the item they asked about. A template that says 'Dear customer, your query has been received' loses the sale. A template that says 'Sana, the maroon is in stock, Rs 3,850' keeps it.

Do not send the same offer broadcast to everyone in your contacts. People who never asked will report you, and your number can be restricted. Also do not promise 'delivery tomorrow' to close a sale if you cannot deliver tomorrow. One broken promise costs ten future customers.
Practice

Do this now:|Write your first reply template, three lines maximum|Add the five quick replies in WhatsApp Business|Send it to yourself and read it as a customer|Answer every open chat from the last week using the new structure|Note which question comes up most; that becomes your next caption

day-9.t: Day 9 — Editing: cut it until it works

b.v: Today's goal

v: Cut a page by a third without losing meaning
Remove the four kinds of weak words
Read aloud to find what is broken

b.v: About 20 minutes. Bring a real page you have written. Editing teaches faster than writing.
First drafts are always too long. Long copy is not more convincing; it is more skippable. Editing is where the sale is won, because it forces you to keep only what the buyer needs.
1) Cut by a third
Take your page and remove one third of the words. Never remove facts, prices or promises. Remove everything else.

Cut in passes:|Pass 1: delete the first paragraph. It is usually a warm up.|Pass 2: delete every sentence that repeats an earlier idea|Pass 3: replace three word phrases with one word|Pass 4: read aloud. Where you stumble, rewrite.|Pass 5: check every number and price is still correct
2) The four weak words

v: Very, really, extremely = usually removable with no loss", "Quality, premium, best = replace with a fact such as material or years", "Solutions, services, products = say what it actually is", "We believe, we feel, we think = the buyer does not care; state the fact

b.v: Example: 'We provide premium quality stitching solutions' becomes 'We stitch suits in 5 days for Rs 1,200'. Shorter, clearer and easier to believe.
3) Read it as three people
One read is not enough. Read the same page as a rushed buyer, a suspicious buyer, and a buyer comparing you with a competitor.

Three reads:|Rushed: can I find the price in five seconds?|Suspicious: is there any proof, or only claims?|Comparing: what does this page say that the other shop cannot say?|Fix whatever fails. Then read it once aloud on your phone.

Do not use spell check as your only editor, and do not trust a thesaurus to make writing better. Big words hide small thinking. Simple words, exact facts, short lines. Also check names and numbers: a wrong price in a good sentence is still a wrong price.
Practice

Do this now:|Take your longest page and cut a third of the words|Delete the first paragraph completely|Replace every vague word with a fact|Read it aloud and fix the stumbles|Publish the shorter version and note the date

day-10.t: Day 10 — A/B tests, plagiarism and claims you can defend

b.v: Today's goal

v: Run a simple A/B test and read it honestly
Write original copy without copying
Keep every claim provable

b.v: About 25 minutes. Then run one test for two weeks before changing anything else.

Copywriting is a craft with feedback. Without testing you are guessing. With careless claims or copied text you can lose customers, rankings or your account, so the last lesson is about testing well and staying safe.
1) A/B testing in plain words
An A/B test shows two versions to similar people at the same time and compares one result. Change one thing only, or you learn nothing.

Run a clean test:|Pick one element: headline, price line, photo, or first WhatsApp line|Write version A and version B with one clear difference|Decide the result you are measuring: messages, orders, replies|Decide in advance how long you will run it, at least one week|Split traffic or alternate days fairly|Compare the result, not the likes|Keep the winner and write down why you think it won
2) Write original, not borrowed

Copying a competitor's page feels efficient and fails. Their facts are wrong for you, the text competes with the original, and it can be a copyright problem. Copying is also easy to spot: the same sentences appear in two places.

v: Research by reading three competitor pages, then close them before writing", "Write from your own stock, prices and customers", "Use your own photos and your own measurements", "If you quote someone, keep it short and name the source", "Never paste text from a supplier catalogue without rewriting it

b.v: 3) Claims you can defend
A claim is any statement about what your product does. If a customer complained, could you show evidence? If not, soften it or remove it.

v: Say 'helps' instead of 'cures' for anything health related", "Give the conditions: 'colour holds after 10 washes' not 'never fades'", "Avoid 'best', 'number one' and 'guaranteed results' unless you can prove them", "Do not use another brand's name to sell your copy of it", "Keep a folder with the proof for every strong claim you make

b.v: Do not make medical, financial or legal claims you are not qualified to make. 'This supplement cures diabetes' is both dangerous and illegal in most places. Describe what the product is and what it does, and let a qualified professional advise the customer on their condition.
Practice

Finish with this:|Choose one element to test this week|Write version B and set the end date|Check every strong claim on your main page and keep proof for each|Rewrite one sentence that copies a competitor's phrasing|Add a note to your calendar to read the test result on the end date
